Item-Restscore Association Conditional on the Total Score

Source: R/brms_fitstats.R
item_restscore_statistic.Rd

Computes the item-restscore association (Kreiner, 2011) for Rasch-family models fitted with brms, with a posterior predictive check that conditions on each person's total score. The observed Goodman-Kruskal gamma between each item and its rest-score (total score minus that item) is compared with (i) its expected value under the model, conditional on the total scores, and (ii) the gammas of datasets replicated conditional on the total scores. Both are computed for each posterior draw of the item parameters.

Usage

item_restscore_statistic(
  model,
  item_var = item,
  person_var = id,
  ndraws_use = NULL
)

Arguments

model

A fitted brmsfit object from a Rasch-family model in which the total score is sufficient for the person location: family = acat (partial credit or rating scale model) or family = bernoulli() (dichotomous Rasch model), both with the logit link, a person random intercept (1 | id), and no disc term. Other models stop with an error.

item_var

An unquoted variable name identifying the item grouping variable in the model data (e.g., item).

person_var

An unquoted variable name identifying the person grouping variable in the model data (e.g., id).

ndraws_use

Optional positive integer. If specified, a random subset of posterior draws of this size is used. If NULL (the default), all draws are used.

Value

A list with two elements:

result

A tibble with one row per item, sorted by gamma_diff in decreasing order, and the columns:

item

The item identifier, named after item_var.

gamma_obs

The observed gamma between the item and the rest-score.

gamma_exp

The expected gamma conditional on the total scores, as in Kreiner (2011), averaged over posterior draws.

gamma_diff

gamma_obs - gamma_exp.

ppp

Mid-p posterior predictive p-value, the proportion of draws where gamma_obs exceeds the replicated gamma, counting ties as one half. Values near 1 indicate stronger association than the model implies, values near 0 weaker.

p_adj

Two-sided posterior predictive p-value adjusted for the number of items by a single-step max-T procedure. See Details.

gamma_rep

Mean of the replicated gamma across draws.

gamma_diff_q025, gamma_diff_q975

95% credible interval for gamma_obs minus the expected gamma. It reflects uncertainty in the item parameters only. See Details.

gamma_diff_q005, gamma_diff_q995

99% credible interval for the same difference.

gamma_rep_q025, gamma_rep_q975

95% posterior predictive interval for the gamma of a replicated dataset.

gamma_rep_q005, gamma_rep_q995

99% posterior predictive interval for the same.

draws

A tibble in long format with one row per item and draw, and the columns item (named after item_var), draw, gamma_rep (replicated gamma) and gamma_exp (expected gamma).

Details

Observed gamma above the expected value means the item discriminates more than the equal discrimination of the Rasch model implies, and observed gamma below it means the item discriminates less.

Under a Rasch-family model the total score is sufficient for the person location. Given the total score, the distribution of a person's responses depends on the item parameters only. For each posterior draw \(s\) the function:

  1. Takes the category probabilities from posterior_epred and removes the person location from them, which leaves item weights that depend on that draw's item parameters only.

  2. Computes, with elementary symmetric functions, the probability of each item score given each person's total score. Summed over persons, these give the expected item \(\times\) rest-score table and its gamma, \(\gamma^{exp(s)}_i\).

  3. Draws a replicated dataset in which every person keeps their observed total score, and computes the replicated gamma \(\gamma^{rep(s)}_i\).

The observed gamma \(\gamma^{obs}_i\) is computed once from the data. Persons with the minimum or maximum total score carry no information about fit and their responses are reproduced as observed in every replicated dataset.

Because replication conditions on the total scores, the reference distribution does not depend on the person locations. The data are still used to estimate the item parameters, but these are few relative to the number of persons. This removes the main reason why posterior predictive p-values based on person parameters drawn from the same data are conservative (Robins et al., 2000).

The gamma_diff interval describes how far the observed sample departs from the model expectation, given the uncertainty in the item parameters. It contains no sampling variation, so it is not a test, and it is not a credible interval for misfit in the population. Use ppp or p_adj to judge whether a departure is larger than chance would produce. As with any test, they will flag smaller departures as the sample size grows.

p_adj standardises each item's observed gamma by the mean and standard deviation of its replicated gammas. Its reference is the largest absolute standardised deviation across items within each replicated dataset, so it accounts for testing all items at once.

With missing responses, the total and rest-scores are sums over the items a person answered, scored from 0. The conditional distribution is computed for each person's set of answered items.

Replication uses random numbers, so call set.seed() first for reproducible results.

References

Kreiner, S. (2011). A note on item-restscore association in Rasch models. Applied Psychological Measurement, 35(7), 557–561.

Goodman, L. A. & Kruskal, W. H. (1954). Measures of association for cross classifications. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 49(268), 732–764.

Bürkner, P.-C. (2021). Bayesian Item Response Modeling in R with brms and Stan. Journal of Statistical Software, 100, 1–54. doi:10.18637/jss.v100.i05

Robins, J. M., van der Vaart, A. & Ventura, V. (2000). Asymptotic distribution of P values in composite null models. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 95(452), 1143–1156. doi:10.1080/01621459.2000.10474310

See also

item_restscore_post for a summary table and plot, infit_statistic for posterior predictive infit/outfit, q3_statistic for Bayesian Q3 residual correlations, posterior_epred.

Examples

# \donttest{
library(brms)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(tibble)

# --- Partial Credit Model ---

df_pcm <- eRm::pcmdat2 %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ .x + 1)) %>%
  rownames_to_column("id") %>%
  pivot_longer(!id, names_to = "item", values_to = "response")

fit_pcm <- brm(
  response | thres(gr = item) ~ 1 + (1 | id),
  data   = df_pcm,
  family = acat,
  chains = 4,
  cores  = 1, # use more cores if you have
  iter   = 500 # use at least 2000 
)
#> Compiling Stan program...
#> Error in .fun(model_code = .x1): Boost not found; call install.packages('BH')

# Item-restscore association
irs <- item_restscore_statistic(
  model      = fit_pcm,
  ndraws_use = 100 # use at least 500
)
#> Error: object 'fit_pcm' not found

# Post-process draws
irs_results <- item_restscore_post(irs)
#> Error: object 'irs' not found
irs_results$summary
#> Error: object 'irs_results' not found
irs_results$plot
#> Error: object 'irs_results' not found

# --- Dichotomous Rasch Model ---

df_rm <- eRm::raschdat3 %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("id") %>%
  pivot_longer(!id, names_to = "item", values_to = "response")

fit_rm <- brm(
  response ~ 1 + (1 | item) + (1 | id),
  data   = df_rm,
  family = bernoulli(),
  chains = 4,
  cores  = 1, # use more cores if you have
  iter   = 500 # use at least 2000 
)
#> Compiling Stan program...
#> Error in .fun(model_code = .x1): Boost not found; call install.packages('BH')

irs_rm <- item_restscore_statistic(
  model      = fit_rm,
  ndraws_use = 100 # use at least 500
)
#> Error: object 'fit_rm' not found

# Post-process draws
irs_results <- item_restscore_post(irs_rm)
#> Error: object 'irs_rm' not found
irs_results$summary
#> Error: object 'irs_results' not found
irs_results$plot
#> Error: object 'irs_results' not found
# }
